remit_rules.excerpt: MUST refuse to dispatch work, relay output, or resolve approvals until an operator-configured allowlist is set.
On an enabled network-exposed adapter with no caller allowlist, the response MUST be fail-closed
Callers outside the configured authorization set
MUST default to a loopback bind; MUST require an allowlist before serving.

threats.summary: Any WeCom/Weixin/QQBot user dispatches terminal-capable agent work because the default open dm_policy plus enforces_own_access_policy skips gateway default-deny.
A sender forging an allowlisted From address on email passes EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS with no DKIM/DMARC check and drives the agent.
Webhook, WeCom-callback, MS Graph, LINE and Teams receivers listen on 0.0.0.0 by default, exposing signature-validation code to the network without an operator bind decision.
An unallowlisted sender on adapters that do not claim their own access policy (Telegram, Slack, Discord, ...) is refused before dispatch.

trust_boundaries.name: Ingested web, file and MCP content into context

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT act on instructions embedded in ingested content

threats.summary: Attacker-authored instructions in read_file output, email bodies and terminal output enter context unlabeled, and web/MCP delimiters can be closed early because the closing tag is not escaped.

trust_boundaries.name: Desktop app to local agent API server

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST bind loopback only and rely on OS-level access control

threats.summary: Another local process or network caller drives the terminal-capable API server without credentials; the server refuses to start without API_SERVER_KEY and defaults to 127.0.0.1.
Credentials surfaced in terminal output are forwarded to the provider in tool results; terminal output is regex-redacted before returning to the loop.
threats.remainder: Redaction is pattern-based and is switched off by security.redact_secrets: false in config.yaml (agent/redact.py:334).

remit_rules.excerpt: Destructive or irreversible shell and file operations ... MUST require operator approval before execution, in every execution context
On a destructive-command match, the response MUST be halt-pending-approval
any untrusted input surface MUST run under a sandboxed terminal backend (Docker/Modal/Daytona) or whole-process wrapping
terminal / shell execution, file read / write / patch, code execution, web search / fetch, browser control, MCP client tools

threats.summary: Destructive commands run without approval in oneshot (forced yolo) and other non-interactive contexts, and write_file/patch overwrite files with no gate.
Injected instructions drive host shell commands on the default local backend; commands outside the regex denylist run with no prompt and nothing rejects untrusted ingress on that backend.
computer_use (GUI control) and ha_call_service (physical device actuation) are in the shared core toolset outside the remit baseline and activate once prerequisites exist.

trust_boundaries.name: Credentials at rest and in subprocess environments

remit_rules.excerpt: the strip set MUST cover every configured provider/gateway credential
Credentials MUST NOT be written into the main config file or into version control
Operator credentials and session authorization material MUST NOT egress to any destination outside the trust envelope

threats.summary: WeCom, Weixin, DingTalk, Feishu, LINE and Teams secrets are absent from the terminal env denylist and are inherited by every shell command.
Custom-endpoint and auxiliary-model flows write the operator's API key in plaintext into config.yaml.
Provider and gateway credentials reach MCP stdio subprocesses; prevented by an OS-variable allowlist plus explicitly configured env.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent writes to its own control configuration

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT disable, bypass, or route around its own safety controls (approval gate, output redaction, caller allowlists, credential scoping)
The agent MUST NOT grant itself new authority beyond what the operator has explicitly granted

threats.summary: The agent runs `hermes config set approvals.mode off` through the terminal (not in DANGEROUS_PATTERNS), persistently disabling the approval gate for all later actions.
The agent overwrites config.yaml or auth.json with write_file/patch to change its controls; Hermes control files are on the write denylist for active and root profiles.

trust_boundaries.name: Memory and self-authored skills replayed into prompts

threats.summary: Injected content is saved to MEMORY.md/USER.md past a regex-only scan, or into agent-authored skills that skip Skills Guard by default, and reloads into every later session.

remit_rules.excerpt: Outbound telemetry and usage attribution are opt-in and off by default
Any outbound destination reached in code but absent from the operator's configured/allowlisted set is a trust expansion
Tool invocations, approval decisions, and session lifecycle events MUST be recorded to durable, structured logs

threats.summary: Official desktop builds send screen views, feature usage and an anonymous ID to PostHog by default because consent defaults to enabled when the build-time key is present.
Approve/deny decisions are not persisted and tool invocations are logged only at DEBUG, so approval incidents cannot be reconstructed.

trust_boundaries.name: Installer, update, dependency and MCP provenance

remit_rules.excerpt: each MUST be reviewed and approved by the operator before install or activation; none may be auto-trusted on the strength of its own description alone
Unreviewed third-party skills, plugins, or MCP servers
installers and runtime updates MUST be integrity-verified before they replace the running app or backend

threats.summary: An MCP server adds or redefines tools mid-session via tools/list_changed with no operator review; poisoned descriptions are only logged.
The desktop first-run installer pipes install.sh/install.ps1 from the mutable main branch into a shell with no hash or signature, and Windows/Linux builds are unsigned.
The catalog n8n MCP manifest installs a third-party repo at ref main and bootstraps unpinned requirements.
Desktop runtime dependencies (electron-updater, posthog-js, ...) are caret-ranged with no dependency or vulnerability scanning in CI.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent output rendered in the desktop UI

remit_rules.excerpt: agent output MUST be treated as inert (displayed as data, never evaluated as HTML/script/markup with side effects)

threats.summary: Injected agent or tool output rendered as active HTML/script in the desktop; react-markdown has no raw-HTML plugin and renderers are sandboxed and context-isolated under a strict CSP.

Default dm_policy 'open' accepts the sender
enforces_own_access_policy short-circuits default-deny
Attacker text becomes the agent's task

attack_paths.name: Forged operator email reaches the host shell

steps.summary: Attacker forges the From header of an allowlisted address
Unverified From address becomes user_id
EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS matches the forged identity
Forged instructions drive the agent as the operator
Non-denylisted commands are not gated
Host command runs and can read inherited gateway secrets

attack_paths.name: Poisoned web page plants instructions in long-term memory

steps.summary: Attacker-authored page content is fetched
Delimiter wrap is closable because the closing tag is not escaped
Injected instructions steer the model
Instruction saved to memory or an unscanned agent-authored skill, reloaded every session

attack_paths.name: Rug-pulled MCP server turns off the approval gate for good

steps.summary: Server redefines tools via list_changed; poisoned descriptions only logged
Poisoned tool definition enters the model's tool schema and steers it
'hermes config set approvals.mode off' is not a dangerous pattern
Command runs unprompted
approvals.mode off persisted; every later check auto-approves

attack_paths.name: Poisoned web page exfiltrates gateway secrets through the shell

steps.summary: Attacker-authored page content is fetched
Labeling is a model-obedience hint only

env/curl-style commands are not on the denylist
Unstripped WeCom/Weixin/DingTalk/Feishu tokens in the subprocess env egress via the command
